keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1018-1055: Bhoja's empire 'extended from Chittor in the north to upper Konkan in the south, and from the Sabarmati River in the west to Vidisha in the east' (Bhoja page). Lata is added (c. 1018 invasion) and upper Konkan ('captured Konkana sometime between 1018 and 1020'); the page's Konkan was 'lost to the Chalukyas of Kalyani' by the end of his reign (1055). The Sabarmati and Chittor limits are inside the 980 shape or add little; the rest of the claim (Kailasha to Malaya) the page calls 'an obvious exaggeration'. Repair of 2026-10-19: Lata is Lata proper, as in the ledger (gain 1018, loss 1056); Konkan is the Mumbai disc (68 cells), 67 of which Cliopatria's Western Chalukya shapes hold from 980 and which the Western Chalukya dossier now loses to this one in 1020.

203,216 km2 for 1056-1110: the corrected 980 shape (Cliopatria's 53-cell drop is the Shakambhari-Ajmer country, given to the Chauhan Dynasty row). Bhoja died in 1055; the Chaulukya Bhima I and the Kalachuri Karna 'attacked his kingdom' (Bhoja page) and the page records the loss of Konkan to the Chalukyas of Kalyani; no further land is named. Lata proper was lost in 1056 to the Kalachuris (ledger; Chaulukya page: 'Meanwhile, the Kalachuris managed to capture the Lata region'), which is why this shape lacks it. Cliopatria's shape holds only 2 cells of the Lata discs.

196,333 km2: 33 more cells lost in the south of Rajasthan (24.5 N, 73.6 E, in the Chaulukya 1111 shape): the Jayasimha page has his control 'extended to parts of present-day Rajasthan' and the Paramara page has Naravarman (1094-1133) lose land 'to the Chandelas and to Jayasimha Siddharaja'. The shape is right to 1135 only: 'Jayasimha's conquest of the Paramara capital Dhara can be dated to 1135-1136' and Malwa is not Paramara again before the 1170s-1192.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1111 shape without Malwa: a rump outside Malwa, unverified

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1136-1177: Malwa lost. 'During 1135-1136 CE, Jayasimha annexed the Paramara kingdom of Malwa' (Chaulukya page); Jayavarman I regained Dhara in 1142-1143 and lost it to the usurper Ballala; 'The Chaulukya king Kumarapala defeated Ballala around 1150 CE. Malwa then became a province of the Chaulukyas' (Paramara page); the table lists an 'Interregnum 1143-1175'. What remains is unknown; the rump drawn is Cliopatria's shape outside the Malwa region (Rajasthan and the Bundelkhand edge), which no page confirms. Jayavarman I page (opened 2026-10-19) does not confirm this rump: it says the Chaulukyas 'had captured a large part of the Paramara kingdom' (1138 Ujjain inscription), 'the Paramara royals appear to have moved to the area around present-day Bhopal' (Chandrapuri, Badnawar and Barkheda are named, no years), that Ballala was 'king of Dhara in the 1160 Veraval inscription', that the Chaulukyas 're-occupied the Paramara territory in the 1150s', and that 'Sometime before 1190, Jayavarman's son Vindhyavarman regained control of a substantial part of the former Paramara territory'. The Bhopal area lies inside the Malwa region the shape removes, so the rump drawn here (Cliopatria's shape outside Malwa) stays unverified.

New keyframe 1178-1187: Vindhyavarman 'restored Paramara power' and 'regained control of the capital Dhara by 1192'. R. C. Majumdar dates the recovery to the reign of Mularaja II (c. 1175-1178); A. K. Majumdar holds that Malwa 'remained under Chaulukya control during Mularaja's reign'. 1178 is used; 1192 is the page's firm bound. The shape is Cliopatria's 1111 shape.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1111 shape: southern Malwa with Dhara stays Paramara

The Seuna page records no annexation from the Paramaras (Simhana's invasion of 1215, Krishna's victory before 1250 and Ramachandra's of the 1270s were 'without territorial gains') and the Vindhyavarman page has Dhara regained 'by 1192'. The 1111 shape is restored; the Yadava dossier should drop the 131 cells.

179,307 km2, the 1202 shape; same correction. Subhatavarman (1194-1209) raided Gujarat and Arjunavarman I (1210-1215) defeated Jayantasimha in Gujarat, then was defeated 'by the Yadava general Kholeshvara in Lata' (Paramara page): raids, no land.

Corrected: the 1111 shape to 1235, then the new keyframe 1236. fx-27: Gwalior, Ranthambore and Mandore subtracted. region.text: Malwa and surrounding areas in west-central India

ledger.note: 948: the Paramaras of Malwa. Infobox 'Established: 948'; the text has them 'established in either the 9th or 10th century' and 'most probably' Rashtrakuta vassals, Siyaka 'a feudatory of the Rashtrakuta ruler Krishna III in his early days' (949). The page names no founder and no town.

region.text: Lata proper, southern Gujarat: the Vadodara and Surat discs without the northern margin (59 cells at 21.2-23.4 N, 72.1-73.7 E) that Cliopatria's 1111-1303 Chaulukya shapes keep and that lies in Gujarat proper

ledger.note: c. 1018: Bhoja takes Lata. 'Around 1018 CE, he defeated the Chalukyas of Lata'; the Bhoja page: 'Bhoja's first military aggression appears to be his invasion of the Lata region ... around 1018 CE' and 'Bhoja subjugated the Chalukyas of Lata, whose ruler Kirtiraja may have served as his feudatory for a brief period'. Chaulukya dossier: Lata is Kirtiraja's from c. 1009 (Chaulukya page: 'Kirtiraja regained control of the region within a short time, before being defeated by the Paramara king Bhoja'), so the counterpart is chalukyas-of-lata and no Chaulukya claim overlaps. Lata is Lata proper: the Vadodara 120 km and Surat 80 km discs without the 59 northern-margin cells that Cliopatria keeps Chaulukya in 1111-1303 (the region shared with chaulukya-dynasty and western-chalukya-empire, repair of 2026-10-19).

1018-1020: Bhoja captures northern Konkan. 'Bhoja invaded and captured Konkana sometime between 1018 and 1020 CE' (Bhoja page: from the Shilahara king Arikesari; 'His 1020 CE inscription states that he organized a Konkana-Grahana Vijaya Parva'; 'The Shilaharas probably continued to administer Konkana as Bhoja's vassals'). Counterpart changed from shilahara-dynasty to western-chalukya-empire in the repair of 2026-10-19: the Shilaharas of the north Konkan were Chalukya feudatories (Satyashraya page: 'Satyashraya however subdued the Shilahara King Aparajita of the northern Konkan'; Shilahara page: 'Rattaraja ... was compelled to transfer his allegiance to Taila II' and 'Soon after the issue of the plates in 1008, the rule of Konkan passed over to the later Chalukyas'), and Cliopatria's Western Chalukya shapes hold these cells from 980. Mirror: western-chalukya-empire /ledger loss 1020. Disagreement: the Jayasimha II page says he 'annexed the northern Konkan and Lata ... for a few years' and was 'to recover all his northern territories by c.1024', while the Bhoja page has Konkan lost only 'by the end of his reign'; the Bhoja page is the specific one and is followed.

region.text: the Shakambhari and Ajmer country that Cliopatria draws as Paramara in 980-1055 and as Chauhan from 1056

ledger.note: c. 1040: Bhoja occupies Shakambhari. 'During the reign of Viryarama (r. c. 1040 CE), the Paramara king Bhoja invaded the Chahamana kingdom' and 'probably occupied their capital Shakambhari for a brief period' (Chahamana page); the Bhoja page: he 'defeated and killed Viryarama'. Hatched, not annexed.
By 1055: Konkan lost. 'By the end of his reign, Bhoja had lost this territory to the Chalukyas of Kalyani' (Bhoja page; 1055 is the last year of the reign).

Naravarman (1094-1133) lost land 'to the Chandelas and to Jayasimha Siddharaja' (Paramara page); the page gives no year or place. Naravarman page reread 2026-10-19: 'Naravarman appears to have suffered at defeat against the Chandelas', the Talwada inscription says Jayasimha 'humbled the pride of Naravarman', he 'also suffered a defeat against the Chahamanas of Shakambhari' (no years or places), and the Ingnoda inscription of 1133-34 shows an independent ruler north-east of Ujjain. Still a confidence-1 bridge; mirror: chaulukya-dynasty /ledger gain 1111.

region.text: Malwa, Dhara and the surrounding areas

ledger.note: 1135-1136: Jayasimha Siddharaja takes Dhara. 'Jayasimha's conquest of the Paramara capital Dhara can be dated to 1135-1136 CE'; the Chaulukya page: he 'annexed the Paramara kingdom of Malwa'. The page does not say how long he held Malwa.
1142: Jayavarman I regains Dhara. Table: Jayavarman I (1142-1143) 'regained Dhara, then lost it to Ballala'. The page gives no month.

1143: the usurper Ballala takes Dhara. Table: Jayavarman I 'regained Dhara, then lost it to Ballala'; the Vindhyavarman page: the kingdom 'was first usurped by one Ballala, and then came under the suzerainty of the Chaulukya dynasty'. The page does not say whether Ballala was a Hoysala. 'Interregnum (usurper Ballala, then Kumarapala) 1143-1175'. Counterpart changed from the free text 'Ballala (usurper)' to 'nobody' (reviewer, 2026-10-19): Ballala is a usurper named once; Jayavarman I page: 'Some years after Jayavarman's ascension, the Paramara territory came under the rule of a person named Ballala', 'the king of Dhara in the 1160 Veraval inscription', 'a former Paramara feudatory, a Hoysala chief, or a governor installed by the Chalukyas of Kalyani'. Malwa is unattributed land 1143-1150 (chaulukya-dynasty /ledger gain 1150 comes from nobody).

Majumdar) and 'having regained control of the capital Dhara by 1192 CE'; A. K. Majumdar 'believes that Malwa remained under Chaulukya control during Mularaja's reign'. The page's own reign dates: Vindhyavarman c. 1175-c. 1194.

region.text: Bhilsa (Vidisha), 23.52 N 77.81 E; the page names Bhilsa only

ledger.note: By 1239 (bridge): Devapala regains Bhilsa. 'Devapala regained it' (Devapala reigned 1215/1218-1239 on the table); the page gives no year. [Reviewer sa-03-f, 2026-10-19] Region moved to Bhilsa, as /ledger/13. Devapala page reread 2026-10-19: 'Iltutmish captured Bhilsa during 1233-34'; 'This indicates that Devapala recaptured Bhilsa' (inferred from a 1263 inscription; no year for the recapture); Devapala reigned c. 1218-1239 and Vagabhata 'killed Devapala and gained control of the Malwa territory'. 1239 stays a bridge.

c. 1255 (bridge): the capital moves from Dhara to Mandapa-Durga (Mandu), 'after Dhara was sacked multiple times'. 'Either Jaitugi or Jayavarman II moved the Paramara capital': the page gives no year, so the change of reign, 1255, is used. Not on the Devapala page (it names neither Dhara nor Mandu); unchanged.

certainty.note: No treaty line appears on any page opened; Bhoja's limits (Chittor, the Sabarmati, Vidisha, upper Konkan) are scholars' readings of inscriptions, and Dhara changed hands several times. The shapes are Cliopatria's approximations.

notes:
Settled: founding 948 (infobox), the Cliopatria row ending 1235 against the page's 1305, Dhara lost 1135-1136 and regained by 1192, Konkan and Lata under Bhoja, Bhilsa 1233-34.
Disagreements and gaps: (1) The Paramara shapes 1188-1235 omit southern Malwa (131 cells inside Cliopatria's Yadava Dynasty row from 1188); the Seuna page records no annexation from the Paramaras and the Vindhyavarman page has Dhara regained by 1192. The yadava-dynasty dossier should drop those cells. (2) Cliopatria's Mamluk Dynasty row of 1236 covers 699 of 732 cells of the Paramara 1227 shape although the page has the Paramaras ruling to 1305; the sa-04 dossier for mamluk-dynasty should not draw Malwa from 1236. (3) The 1136-1177 rump is Cliopatria's shape outside Malwa, which no page confirms; Majumdar's two readings of the recovery (c.1175-1178 vs 'by 1192') are both on the Vindhyavarman page. (4) The Ballala who usurped Malwa (1143-c.1150) is named by no other detail; counterpart 'Ballala (usurper)' needs no dossier. (5) Lata under Bhoja overlaps the Chaulukya shape; both dossiers keep Lata. (6) Dates of the Shilahara conquest rest on 'between 1018 and 1020'; the counterpart name is mine. (7) Madanavarman's capture of Bhilsa 'on the western periphery of the Paramara kingdom' and Lakshmivarman's recapture (Chandela page) are undated and not drawn. (8) 1255 capital move is a bridge. Counterparts without a dossier: chalukyas-of-lata, shilahara-dynasty (northern Konkan), Ballala (usurper). Gazetteer: 'Dhara' / 'Dhar' (22.60 N 75.30 E) and 'Mandu' exist only as place Mandu; 'Dhar' is missing. Pages (5): Paramara dynasty, Bhoja, Jayasimha Siddharaja, Vindhyavarman, Seuna dynasty; the Chahamana and Chaulukya pages were opened for those dossiers.

Repair 2026-10-19 (after the adversarial review of sa-03-f, verdict fail; the reviewer's own fix of /ledger/13, /ledger/14 and /wars/8 to a 60 km disc at Bhilsa is kept). (1) Lata: gain 1018 from chalukyas-of-lata, loss 1056 to kalachuris-of-tripuri (confidence 1; Chaulukya page 'Meanwhile, the Kalachuris managed to capture the Lata region', Karna page: the general Vapullaka), with the same region (Lata proper, 147 cells) as chaulukya-dynasty and western-chalukya-empire; the Chaulukya dossier no longer holds Lata for 1009-1073, so the double claim of 1018-1055 is gone. (2) Konkan: counterpart western-chalukya-empire (Shilahara vassals of the Chalukyas), which now carries the mirror loss of 1020; the Jayasimha II page's 'recover all his northern territories by c.1024' disagrees with the Bhoja page's 'lost this territory by the end of his reign' (1055): the Bhoja page is followed. (3) 'Ballala (usurper)' became 'nobody'; the war's belligerent keeps the name. (4) Thin items looked at: the 1111 south-Rajasthan loss is still unplaced (Naravarman page: defeats by Chandelas, Jayasimha and Chahamanas, no years or places; mirrored in chaulukya-dynasty); the Bhilsa dates stay bridges (Devapala page); the 1136-1177 rump is not confirmed (Jayavarman I page: royals around Bhopal); no page gives the extent for 1236-1304 (Paramara page not reopened: the Devapala and Jayavarman I pages add nothing). Newly learned, not drawn: Madanavarman of the Chandelas was at Bhilsa in 1134 (Augasi inscription, Madanavarman page) and Lakshmivarman recaptured the region by 1143-44, which would be a Paramara loss and regain of Bhilsa under Naravarman and Yashovarman; an open event pair.
